thesis: Measure how workflow and runtime changes affect time to a correct, authorized outcome.

functional.name: Correctness and control checks
functional.question: Does each input reach the right outcome, including rejection, review and replay?

latency.name: Repeated latency comparison
latency.question: Does one change reduce observed completion time at the same offered load?

deadline.name: Repeated deadline comparison
deadline.question: How much correct work finishes before the declared deadline?

baseline.name: Repeated baseline
baseline.question: How repeatable is this declared workload before changing a factor?

endurance.name: Endurance / soak
endurance.question: Does the declared load remain correct over an extended observation?

capacity.name: Load and capacity qualification
capacity.question: Which tested offered rates satisfy the full acceptance contract?

population.name: Finite-population scaling
population.question: How does completion time change when a burst targets more waiting workflows?

recovery.name: Fault and recovery checks
recovery.question: What happens to state and business effects during a specific injected failure?

measurement.name: Measurement diagnostics
measurement.question: How do observation and instrumentation settings affect what the harness reports?

reading_rules: Every comparison has its own baseline. Different workloads, hosts or databases cannot be combined into one speedup.
Correctness and speed answer different questions. A correctly refused payment can pass the test but does not count as a settlement.
Observed p95 is the latency below which 95% of observed completions fall. It includes the declared observer boundary; it is not the slowest request or a pure engine timer.
Deadline goodput counts correct outcomes within the deadline per second. Offered load counts starts requested per second. Neither alone establishes maximum capacity.
Paired changes compare matched runs. A median of five changes is not a pooled percentile, and a range is not a confidence interval.
Keep every miss, retry, interruption and invalid observation. Partial or resource-constrained results cannot be promoted to a completed capacity claim.
Synthetic workflows expose controlled mechanisms. Customer traffic, live models, human time and complete cost per correct outcome require separate studies.

studies.name: Six basic workflow patterns
studies.question: Can the engine start, persist data, coordinate external work, route decisions and protect a synthetic payment?
studies.control: Declared input and independently expected outcome
studies.change: No performance treatment in this record
studies.held_fixed: The BPMN, payload and expected-outcome rules for each case.
studies.population: Minimal, variables, async, KYC, risk and settlement cases.
studies.environment: Local Java/H2 lab or separately qualified OCI deployment.
studies.metric: Correct branch, durable values and exact expected effects.
studies.clock: Functional completion and state checks; no aggregate speedup.
studies.result: Reusable workflows and golden checks define the basic test vocabulary.
studies.meaning: These are small building blocks a workflow developer can combine and extend.
studies.limits: A diagram alone is not a completed performance study. The six basic patterns do not each have a repeated latency comparison.

studies.name: Async reference baseline
studies.question: Is the external-task/echo path repeatable at the declared load?
studies.held_fixed: Synthetic inputs, policy, worker count, resources, database and completion observer within each pair.
studies.metric: Observed p95, correctness and correct completions within two seconds.
studies.clock: Scheduled arrival to durable-history completion observation. Completion polling is part of this measurement. Polling: 100 ms.
studies.result: 90,000/90,000 correct and within two seconds; per-run p95 245.7–249.0 ms.
studies.meaning: This establishes a repeatable reference for this workflow and setup.
studies.limits: The echo workload contains no payment or live model. This is not maximum capacity or an engine-only microbenchmark.

studies.name: Worker pacing under bursts
studies.question: Does an unnecessary pause after successful work delay later payments?
studies.change: Fetch immediately after success; keep idle/retry backoff
studies.held_fixed: Synthetic inputs, policy, worker count, resources, database and completion observer within each pair.
studies.population: 20 arrivals in a one-second burst every ten seconds; mean 2/s. 120-second warmup and 120-second measurement per arm.
studies.environment: Shared OCI controller compute with separate PostgreSQL; one worker.
studies.metric: Correct payments within two seconds; median paired timely-goodput change.
studies.clock: Scheduled arrival to durable-history completion observation. Completion polling is part of this measurement.
studies.result: Timely payments rose from 600/1,200 to 1,200/1,200. All 2,400 outcomes were correct.
studies.meaning: Avoidable worker waiting can consume the deadline even when the payment logic is unchanged.
studies.limits: The control reconstructs an earlier worker setting. It is not the current default or a customer production baseline.

studies.name: Independent payment checks
studies.question: Can independent KYC and risk checks overlap without weakening payment checks?
studies.change: Parallel KYC and risk, with a join before settlement
studies.held_fixed: Synthetic inputs, policy, worker count, resources, database and completion observer within each pair.
studies.population: Approved synthetic payments at 1/s. KYC waits 400 ms; risk waits 600 ms. 2-minute warmup and 10-minute measurement per arm.
studies.environment: Shared OCI controller and separate PostgreSQL; two worker slots.
studies.metric: Median of paired percentage changes in observed completion p95.
studies.clock: Scheduled arrival to durable-history completion observation. Completion polling is part of this measurement. Polling: 100 ms.
studies.result: Observed p95 was 32.1% lower at the median paired change. All 6,000 outcomes were correct and within two seconds.
studies.meaning: Overlap independent waits while preserving the requirement that both checks finish.
studies.limits: Both arms still delivered 1 timely payment/s. This establishes lower latency at this load, not higher maximum capacity or real-provider latency.

studies.name: Different outcomes and dependency delays
studies.question: Does the parallel-check result hold across settlements, refusals and safe stops?
studies.held_fixed: Synthetic inputs, policy, worker count, resources, database and completion observer within each pair.
studies.population: Five dependency profiles and mixed expected outcomes at 1/s; 600 measured arrivals per arm.
studies.metric: Timely correct settlements/s, with refusals and safe stops reported separately.
studies.clock: Scheduled arrival to durable-history completion observation. Completion polling is part of this measurement. Polling: 100 ms.
studies.result: Timely settlements rose from 880 to 1,037 of 1,200; timely refusals fell from 780 to 669 of 1,200. All 6,000 outcomes were correct; 1,648 deadlines were missed.
studies.meaning: A change can help one outcome class and hurt another. Keep the outcome breakdown.
studies.limits: Equal synthetic coverage is not a customer traffic distribution. The approved-only 32.1% result cannot be applied to this mix.

studies.name: Policy-based review routing
studies.question: Can a fixed policy remove unnecessary review tasks while retaining required reviews?
studies.change: Route only policy-required cases to review
studies.held_fixed: Same ten inputs, decision policy, authenticated reviewer checks and final outcome verifier.
studies.population: Ten synthetic cases in each arm.
studies.repeats: One execution of each case per arm; replay probes separately retained.
studies.metric: Review-task count and correct expected outcomes.
studies.clock: Scripted reviews; human waiting or working time is not measured.
studies.result: Review tasks fell from 10 to 4. All four mandatory reviews remained and all 20 expected outcomes passed.
studies.meaning: This workflow removes avoidable handoffs for the declared policy and case mix.
studies.limits: This is a task-count comparison, not measured human time or a 60% staffing saving. The all-review control is deliberately constrained.

studies.name: Parallel FX quote requests
studies.question: Can parallel requests to three independent quote providers improve timely settlement?
studies.change: Request the same quotes in parallel before selection
studies.held_fixed: Synthetic inputs, policy, worker count, resources, database and completion observer within each pair. Three worker slots in both arms.
studies.population: 22 cases × three delay profiles; 396 measured arrivals per arm at 0.5/s. 132-second warmup, 792-second measurement and 30-second drain.
studies.environment: Shared OCI controller and separate PostgreSQL 17.6.
studies.metric: Median paired change in correct settlements within two seconds per second.
studies.clock: Scheduled arrival to durable-history completion observation. Completion polling is part of this measurement. Polling: 100 ms.
studies.result: Timely settlements rose from 668/1,530 to 1,530/1,530. All 3,960 outcomes were correct. Parallel runs retained 910 cached backend replays and zero duplicate payment effects.
studies.meaning: Overlapping quote waits helps delayed-provider cases. Durable replay handling protects the payment when completion retries occur.
studies.limits: Sequential runs had zero cached replays. The parallel improvement has a retry tradeoff. Synthetic providers and equal case coverage do not represent a live FX venue or customer distribution.

studies.name: Java 21 versus Java 25
studies.status: Completed; earlier stopped study remains separate
studies.question: Does the newer Java runtime improve this fixed async workflow?
studies.held_fixed: Synthetic inputs, policy, worker count, resources, database and completion observer within each pair. Fluxnova 3.0.1 fixed.
studies.population: 10 starts/s; 10-minute warmup and 30-minute measurement per observation.
studies.environment: Same fixed OCI reference and PostgreSQL.
studies.metric: Median within-pair observed-p95 difference, Java 25 minus Java 21.
studies.clock: Scheduled arrival to durable-history completion observation. Completion polling is part of this measurement. Polling: 100 ms before deadline, 1,000 ms afterward.
studies.result: Median paired p95 difference: −0.862 ms, range −1.369 to +0.864 ms. All 180,000 outcomes were correct and within two seconds.
studies.meaning: The small differences changed sign. This workload did not establish a broad Java 25 performance advantage.
studies.limits: Five pairs do not prove equivalence, maximum capacity or performance for other workflows. Earlier interrupted observations are not pooled.

studies.name: Fluxnova 3.0.1 versus 3.1.1
studies.status: Completed; earlier stopped study remains separate
studies.question: Does the engine release change this async workflow at the same load?
studies.change: Fluxnova 3.1.1 with its required PostgreSQL migration
studies.held_fixed: Synthetic inputs, policy, worker count, resources, database and completion observer within each pair. Java 21 fixed.
studies.population: 10 starts/s; 10-minute warmup and 30-minute measurement per observation.
studies.environment: Same fixed OCI reference; release-specific native schemas.
studies.clock: Scheduled arrival to durable-history completion observation. Completion polling is part of this measurement. Polling: 100 ms.
studies.result: Median paired p95 difference: +0.126 ms, range −0.552 to +1.055 ms. All 180,000 outcomes were correct and within two seconds.
studies.meaning: Both releases met this test target. No meaningful speedup or capacity gain was established.
studies.limits: This does not prove statistical equivalence, universal compatibility or production sizing. Native schema changes are part of the declared treatment.

studies.name: Eight-hour async endurance
studies.question: Does this workload stay correct through an eight-hour observation?
studies.change: Extend the observation to eight hours
studies.held_fixed: Synthetic inputs, policy, worker count, resources, database and completion observer within each pair.
studies.metric: Correctness, deadline outcomes and descriptive time windows.
studies.clock: Scheduled arrival to durable-history completion observation. Completion polling is part of this measurement.
studies.result: All 288,000 measured workflows completed correctly within two seconds.
studies.meaning: The reference sustained its declared target during this observation.
studies.limits: One observation does not establish leak-free operation, maximum capacity or a production availability guarantee.

studies.name: Higher-rate confirmation
studies.question: Does the next offered rate satisfy the complete confirmation series?
studies.change: Higher offered rates with unchanged acceptance rules
studies.held_fixed: Synthetic inputs, policy, worker count, resources, database and completion observer within each pair.
studies.repeats: Five planned observations: three measured passes, one warmup interruption, one unattempted.
studies.metric: Full-series correctness, deadlines, resources and retained interruptions.
studies.clock: Scheduled arrival to durable-history completion observation. Completion polling is part of this measurement.
studies.result: The 16/s confirmation is incomplete. 16/s is not qualified.
studies.meaning: Three passing observations cannot stand in for a complete five-observation confirmation.
studies.limits: Maximum sustainable capacity remains open. Do not label a discovery rate or partial confirmation as production capacity.

studies.name: Messages, signals and asynchronous batches
studies.status: 45 cells complete; two headroom flags retained
studies.question: How does completion grow when the same pattern targets more waiting workflows?
studies.held_fixed: Engine, database, client limits, 100 ms observer and independent outcome rules.
studies.population: Three patterns × three populations × five repeats. 16,650 measured recipients; 180 controls.
studies.environment: One OCI engine container, one generator/observer and separate PostgreSQL.
studies.metric: Interval bounding cohort completion, with generator/resource qualification.
studies.clock: Delivery start until all intended recipient completions are observed; HTTP acknowledgment and batch bookkeeping are separate.
studies.result: All 16,650 measured recipients were correct. 43/45 cells passed the headroom gate; batch/1,000 timing comparisons remain unqualified.
studies.meaning: Larger finite bursts take longer. Correct final outcomes alone do not qualify every timing comparison.
studies.limits: Different routing semantics cannot be ranked as interchangeable implementations. These bursts do not establish arrival-rate capacity, replica scaling or finite ratios when the control interval includes zero.

studies.name: Cluster job faults and replay handling
studies.question: Do job retry and failure paths preserve the intended effects?
studies.change: One and two engine configurations under controlled faults
studies.held_fixed: Original immutable case data, expected state and exact-effect checks.
studies.environment: Local H2 plus one/two engines sharing an OCI controller with a private PostgreSQL container.
studies.repeats: Separate functional configurations; no repeated capacity comparison.
studies.metric: Completed, blocked and waiting states; attempts and exact effects.
studies.clock: Functional state reconciliation, including eight database tables.
studies.result: Each six-case run produced the expected three completed, two blocked and one waiting outcomes, with 12 exact effects.
studies.meaning: The fault cases exercise coordination and idempotency without losing the expected business state.
studies.limits: Shared-host tests do not establish multi-host availability, failover capacity or a managed-database performance advantage.

studies.name: Native job timing qualification
studies.question: Can native job timing records be matched to independently correct outcomes?
studies.change: Qualify scheduled-arrival recording and timing verification
studies.held_fixed: Original input, job identity and exact effects.
studies.repeats: One qualification observation plus six-case fault regression.
studies.metric: Complete timing/outcome joins, successful attempts and exact effects.
studies.clock: Scheduled arrival and native stage records, checked for complete coverage.
studies.result: 20/20 workflows correct, 60 successful attempts and 60 exact effects.
studies.meaning: The timing pipeline is ready for a later controlled performance study.
studies.limits: No resource-qualified performance, replica-scaling or capacity claim follows from this local gate.

studies.name: Agent, reviewer and payment authority
studies.question: Can an agent request work while policy, a reviewer and a verifier retain control over payment?
studies.control: Immutable original payment intent and explicit authority
studies.change: Exercise model/tool requests, review, rejection and tampering paths
studies.held_fixed: Expected authorized effect and binding to the original request.
studies.environment: Separate local/OCI functional studies and bounded live-provider trials.
studies.repeats: Case coverage; no paired agent-versus-rules experiment.
studies.metric: Expected authorization, decision and exact-effect checks; provider errors retained.
studies.clock: Model, review and workflow stages have separate timing boundaries.
studies.result: Functional checks exercise the control boundaries. A measured agent-versus-rules benefit remains unestablished.
studies.meaning: The workflow decides when actions are allowed; a model suggestion is not payment authority.
studies.limits: Live-provider failures and incomplete coverage remain part of the evidence. These workflow performance percentages are not AI quality or agent-productivity claims.

studies.name: State and dependency recovery
studies.question: Can the declared recovery procedure restore consistent workflow and payment state?
studies.change: Inject selected connection, verifier, key or restore failures
studies.held_fixed: Immutable intent, checkpoint binding and reconciliation rules.
studies.environment: OCI reference and isolated recovery cells.
studies.repeats: Procedure-specific observations, not a general outage distribution.
studies.metric: State preservation, restored readiness and no unauthorized/duplicate effects.
studies.clock: Failure injection, recovery readiness and reconciliation are separate clocks.
studies.result: Evidence covers specific recovery procedures and retained interruptions.
studies.meaning: Recovery must reconcile engine state and payment authority, not only restart a process.
studies.limits: No general availability SLA, universal RTO/RPO or production certification follows from these cases.

studies.name: Polling and worker instrumentation
studies.question: How much does the observation method influence reported latency?
studies.control: Declared observer interval or timing output disabled
studies.change: Change only the observer interval or enable timing output
studies.held_fixed: Workload and environment within each separate diagnostic study.
studies.repeats: Per-study repeats; not pooled with workflow comparisons.
studies.metric: Observed completion delay, request traffic and stage timing coverage.
studies.clock: Observer polling adds detection delay; worker stage records measure a different boundary.
studies.result: Polling and timing settings belong in the experiment contract.
studies.meaning: Faster detection is not automatically faster execution. Keep the measurement method fixed across arms.
studies.limits: These diagnostics are not interchangeable with payment throughput, agent benefit or the later matched workload studies.

patterns.name: Worker pacing
patterns.question: Why wait after a successful task?
patterns.explanation: The payment graph stays the same. The external worker either sleeps after success or immediately fetches the next task. Idle and retry backoff remain.
patterns.interpretation: W01 shows more payments meeting the deadline for fixed bursts and one worker. It tests worker scheduling, not a redesigned payment process.

patterns.name: Parallel checks
patterns.question: Which checks can safely overlap?
patterns.explanation: Sequential execution waits for KYC before starting risk. Parallel execution starts both independent checks and joins them before payment. Neither check is skipped.
patterns.interpretation: W02 shows lower observed latency at 1/s. The mixed follow-up shows that benefits depend on the outcome and dependency delays.

patterns.name: Review routing
patterns.question: Which cases actually need a reviewer?
patterns.explanation: A fixed policy routes required cases to a reviewer. Eligible cases can proceed; unauthorized or unknown cases still stop. Final verification remains.
patterns.interpretation: W03 reduces tasks from ten to four for its constructed cases and preserves all four mandatory reviews. It does not measure human time saved.

patterns.name: Minimal workflow
patterns.question: Can a workflow start and durably finish?
patterns.explanation: Start and finish a process with the declared correlation data and payload. The checker confirms durable completion.
patterns.interpretation: A useful basic readiness check. Its input still contains data, so it is not a zero-variable engine-overhead benchmark.

patterns.name: Variables and branching
patterns.question: Does the right data survive the chosen branch?
patterns.explanation: Choose a branch, cross an asynchronous boundary and inspect persisted values. Persistent and transient data have different expected histories.
patterns.interpretation: Correctness requires the right branch and right surviving values. No separate repeated speedup claim belongs to this picture.

patterns.name: External task and tool
patterns.question: Can the engine, worker and tool finish together?
patterns.explanation: Fluxnova creates an external task. A worker fetches it, calls the deterministic echo tool and reports completion. The benchmark observes durable history.
patterns.interpretation: This is the workload behind P01, the runtime/release comparisons and the soak. Their clocks include worker/tool work and observation.

patterns.name: KYC decision and review
patterns.question: Does each screening result reach the right route?
patterns.explanation: Synthetic screening approves, rejects or creates a review wait. The test simulates completion of that review.
patterns.interpretation: A correct waiting or rejected state can be a passing test. Real screening quality and human working time remain outside this basic fixture.

patterns.name: Risk and freshness
patterns.question: Do limits and stale data prevent the wrong action?
patterns.explanation: Check a synthetic risk limit and market-data freshness. Accept only when both declared conditions allow it.
patterns.interpretation: An expected refusal is correct work, but it is not a settled payment. Report those populations separately.

patterns.name: Settlement and replay
patterns.question: Is the authorized payment effect exact and unique?
patterns.explanation: Check policy before the synthetic ledger effect. Repeating an operation must preserve its original result without paying again.
patterns.interpretation: Successful HTTP responses are insufficient: the checker matches amount, beneficiary and effect count to the original intent. No real money moves.
